result.topic_en: The page evaluates the integral of x^μ/(1+x) from 0 to ∞ by contour integration around a branch cut, then extends the result to complex μ = α + λi; a pencil sketch of a function graph with asymptotes fills the other half.
result.transcription:
$\int_0^\infty \frac{x^\mu\,\partial x}{1+x}$ \quad $x = r e^{\varphi i}$
$\int \frac{(-x)^\mu\,\partial x}{1+x}$ \quad $\frac{x^{\mu+1}}{1+x}\,\frac{\partial x}{x}$ \quad $0 > \mu > -1$ reell[?]
$e^{\log(-x)\mu}$ \quad $x^\mu$
$\log x - \pi i$
$\log x + \pi i$
$\int_0^\infty \frac{x^\mu\,\partial x}{1+x}\left(e^{-\mu\pi i} - e^{\mu\pi i}\right) = 2\pi i$
$\int_\varepsilon^R + \int_R + \int_R^\varepsilon + \int_\varepsilon$
$-\int_\varepsilon^R$ \quad $\frac{e^{2\lambda\pi} + e^{-2\lambda\pi}}{2}$
$\mu = \alpha + \lambda i$
$[-\frac{\pi}{\sin\mu\pi}-] = \frac{2\pi i}{2}$[?]
$\frac{\pi}{\sin(\alpha+\lambda i)\pi} = \frac{\pi\cdot 2\,(\sin\alpha\pi\cos\lambda i\pi - \cos\alpha\pi\sin\lambda i\pi)}{\cos 2\lambda i\pi - \cos 2\alpha\pi}$
[pencil sketch: graph of curves with a horizontal axis, vertical asymptotes and loops; a contour diagram with small circles around $-1$ and $0$, a cut along the axis and a large arc of radius $R$]

methods.what: Contour integration with a keyhole contour around the branch cut to evaluate a Mellin-type integral
Branch values of the logarithm on the two sides of the cut
Residue result for the integral of x^μ/(1+x), equivalent to π/sin(μπ) up to sign
Separation of π/sin((α+λi)π) into real and imaginary parts using sin(a+b)sin(a−b) = (cos 2b − cos 2a)/2
Expression of cos of an imaginary argument as a hyperbolic cosine
